The present claim petition arises out of road accident that occurred on 02.01.2021, in which one Indresh Sharma @ Indresh Kumar (aged about 46 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 02.01.2021 at about 03:20 PM, Sh.Indresh Sharma along with his wife Ms. Pavan Devi travelling on a motorcycle bearing no.UP-16BW-8906.

When they reached in front of Nagar Palika, a Tractor bearing no.UP14GT-8127 (hereinafter referred as to offending vehicle), came at a very high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle.
Due to this impact, they fell on road in where Pavan Kumari died on the spot while Indresh Sharma sustained grievous injuries.

Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet before concerned criminal court while a claim petition was filed by the husband of victim in the present case before this Tribunal.

Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law,
proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.
Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors.

sentences.text: Page no. 6 of 9ss a holistic view has to be taken.
10. In the present case, petitioner has has categorically deposed that the accident occurred owing to the rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1.

In his reply, respondent no.1 has not denied the occurrence of accident or involvement of the Tractor but has pleaded that the accident occurred due to sudden application of brakes by petitioner no.1, whose motorcycle was plying ahead of the offending vehicle.
Respondent no.1 has however not lead any evidence or even examined himself to prove the circumstances in which accident occurred.

It can be gathered from the facts that the offending vehicle must have been driven at such a high speed that it could not apply brakes timely and dashed into the motorcycle ahead of it, which strongly suggests negligence on the part of respondent no.1.
The record further proves that the accident was reported without any inordinate delay.

11. Further, after investigation, even the police had filed chargesheet against respondent no.1 u/s 279/338/304A/427 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident.

In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
Issue no. 2 2. Whether the injured is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
13.

In the instant case insurance company/respondent no.3 has raised a statutory defence pleading that while the offending vehicle was registered as a commercial vehicle, the same was being used as a goods carrying vehicle, it has been argued that the offending vehicle was only insured under miscellaneous carrying comprehensive policy and not under 'Goods Carrying vehicle policy".
It is thus argued that insurance company is not liable.

It is an admitted fact that the offending vehicle which was a tractor was having trolley attached to it,
at the time of accident.

Though, insurance company has examined one Ayush Singh, Manager as R3W1, no evidence has been led by insurance company to prove if such trolley actually carried any goods or that the accident occurred due to the trolley attached to the tractor.
It is not denied that the accident was caused by the front part of the vehicle i.e. tractor itself and not by the trolley.

In such circumstances, it would be immaterial whether or not, the MACT no.86/21 Indresh Sharma @
Indresh Kumar vs. Rajender Prasad & ors. Page no. 8 of 9ss offending vehicle was being used for carrying goods or any other purpose in as much as such annexure to the tractor is not even involved in the accident and no evidence has been led by insurance company to prove that the accident occurred due to trolley attached to the Tractor.

entities.text:
MACT no.86/21 Indresh Sharma @
Indresh Kumar vs. Rajender Prasad & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In absence of any nexus being established between the accident and the trolley or the alleged use of offending vehicle, the defence raised by insurance company is untenable and no breach of policy is proved.
As such, respondent no.3 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
14. As regards the issue of compensation, it is seen from record that petitioner has neither filed any MLC or any other medical document to prove that he sustained any injury.
No medical bill has either been filed to prove expenditure on treatment.
In absence of any proof of injury sustained by the petitioner, no compensation can be awarded under any head.
Issue no.2 is accordingly decided.
